sub_scenario.one_line: technical illustrator: sign, with the workstation clause intact

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the linework files and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The figure queue review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Concept sketching and client markup sessions happen happily at any table.
The loose phases are portable.
Fully portable.
Someone new shadowed me in the drawing station this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the print tolerances into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

My precision linework holds print tolerance because of the fixed workstation rig, calibrated monitor, mounted tablet, locked chair height; the two catalog projects done on that rig shipped without a single redraw request.
The rig is the tolerance record.
The rig is the whole record.
Short correction passes on existing figures tolerate any temporary desk.
Small work travels fine.
Fine and often.
I archived last cycle's notes on the figure queue and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Redraw requests are billed back against the illustrator under the standard studio contract terms.
Failure costs land on you personally.
Personally and per figure.
A vendor call about the linework files ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the drawing station checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the print tolerances.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the figure queue records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The studio contract on offer includes a dedicated fixed-workstation clause naming my rig requirements; the studio wrote the clause after seeing the catalog work.
The contract encodes your mechanism by name.
By name and by monitor model.
I sketched next week's plan for the print tolerances before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the linework files updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The contract also brings the studio's anatomy-plate series, the exact work I want more of.
The role content aligns as well.
Aligns perfectly.
I compared two options for the figure queue tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the drawing station handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The studio contract deadline is Friday. Do I sign, and on what condition?
